question: An item is sold to C by B, and then to D by C. Both B and C earn an equal profit of 12%, and the selling price to D is ₹313.60. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item to B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive profit ⇒ multiply factors

Each gain = 12% ⇒ factor = 1.12

Total factor = 1.12 × 1.12 = 1.2544

CP of B = 313.60 ÷ 1.2544

**∴ Answer = 250**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Both B and C gain 12%, Final SP = 313.60

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + profit/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP of B = x

⇒ B sells to C: SP₁ = x × 1.12

⇒ C sells to D: SP₂ = x × 1.12 × 1.12

⇒ x × (1.12)² = 313.60

⇒ x × 1.2544 = 313.60

⇒ x = 313.60 ÷ 1.2544 = 250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Profit

Net factor = (1 + p/100) × (1 + p/100)

Compound Effect

Profits multiply, not add

Reverse Calculation

CP = Final SP ÷ combined factor
